source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Login BMC ,clear all logs.
2. Check health Led should be green.
3. make a error log (ex: remove one HDD)
4. Check health LED should change to orange/red color.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: make sure your heakth LED status can match status.

original_test_intent: Verify that the physical BMC health LED shows the Project-defined healthy state, transitions to the correct degraded/fault indication for an approved deterministic error such as one safe HDD removal, and returns to healthy after complete recovery.
original_method: Log in to BMC, observe a green baseline LED, create a physical error using HDD removal as the source example, and visually confirm orange/red indication. Preserve the stated log-clearing steps as source text, but export evidence and obtain approval before any clear operation.
manual_activity: A qualified operator identifies the physical LED, performs or supervises the approved fault stimulus, confirms the actual color/blink pattern, handles any drive and verifies physical restoration. Automation may only collect and correlate supporting read-only BMC, SEL, storage and host evidence.
required_inputs: Health LED location and healthy/degraded/critical color plus blink-pattern matrix, severity source, transition timeout, hysteresis and recovery timeout
Approved deterministic fault and corresponding sensor/event/SEL/BMC-health/LED mapping; if HDD is used, exact enclosure/slot/serial/controller/array/member role
Vendor hot-plug/service support, dedicated non-production data set, current array health, redundancy margin, verified backup and rebuild policy
Baseline export and any approved log-clear scope, protected BMC/host access, timestamp/photo method and unexpected-event rules
Operator, abort owner, reinsertion/replacement/rebuild procedure and final restoration criteria
safety_requirements: Do not use the unrelated eight-hour BurnIn workload as evidence for a physical health-LED/storage-fault transition.
Do not remove any boot, mounted, sole-copy, failed, rebuilding, non-redundant or wrong-slot drive; bind the approved physical slot to its serial and array role before action.
Export SEL, BMC and host/storage baselines before any source-requested clear; clearing evidence is a separately approved operation and must not erase pre-existing faults.

Perform only one approved stimulus under attended monitoring; stop on unexpected array state, data risk, wrong LED/event, host loss, additional drive fault, thermal/power anomaly or inability to reinsert.
Do not automatically retry a removal, force an array online, initialize a drive or issue destructive storage commands.

After reinsertion or replacement, keep the case open until the controller recognizes the correct device, rebuild/resync completes if required, data and host health are verified, events clear as specified and the LED returns to the approved healthy indication.
agent_execution_scope: Before execution, validate the approved LED/fault/drive/recovery matrix and collect non-mutating inventory and health baselines only.
During an engineer-performed stimulus, capture timestamped BMC health, SEL, sensor, storage-controller/array and host state and organize independently timestamped LED photos or video.
Correlate healthy, fault and recovered checkpoints, explicitly report any event, LED or timing mismatch and preserve logs.
Do not touch physical storage, clear logs, create a fault, run BurnIn as a substitute, control rebuilds, claim a visual observation, retry or issue PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the exact health-state matrix, safe fault stimulus, drive identity, data protection, evidence and recovery contract.
Perform/supervise physical fault and visual LED checks, control any log clear, reinsertion and rebuild, and stop on safety thresholds.
Verify full storage/data/BMC/LED recovery and issue checkpoint plus final DUT verdicts.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The BurnInTest and SSH proposal belongs to the unrelated row-1524 variant. It neither creates the source's defined health fault nor proves a physical LED transition, and its sshpass/disabled host-key pattern is unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only platform-approved read-only BMC health/LED proxy, sensor/SEL and storage-controller inventory/array queries as supporting evidence around the operator-controlled visual and physical checkpoints.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The green baseline, `orange/red` fault wording, example HDD removal, linked health-monitor script and 10/10-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Define the LED state matrix and one safe stimulus; bind the exact target drive if used; export baseline; observe healthy indication; perform the approved fault once; correlate LED/BMC/SEL/storage evidence; restore the target; complete any rebuild and prove healthy recovery.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Project-specific chassis health LED, BMC health model and storage topology.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record chassis, BMC, CPLD/LED controller, storage controller/backplane, drive and query-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor chassis health-LED severity/state definition, BMC event mapping and approved drive hot-service/rebuild procedure.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds measurable state/timing, exact target identity, baseline preservation, data protection and full recovery while retaining the source's physical LED and fault intent.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A Project-approved synthetic fault may replace HDD removal only if it drives the same BMC health state and LED severity with documented equivalence; BurnIn health logs or read-only LED proxies alone do not cover the physical indication.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: LED matrix, safe stimulus/target, event mapping, recovery and operator approval.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Even a redundant array is degraded during member removal, and a second latent fault can turn a nominal hot-service action into data loss.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may choose a safer approved fault instead of HDD removal or define orange versus red by severity, but must retain the physical LED checkpoint, record the original example, explain equivalent health-model coverage and disclose any untested storage-fault path.
expected_evidence: Preserved row/duplicate identity plus approved LED color/blink/severity/latency/recovery matrix and fault-to-event mapping
Pre-clear exported BMC/SEL/host/storage baseline, chassis and physical LED identity, drive slot/serial/array role and backup/redundancy proof
Operator authorization and timestamped healthy LED visual evidence with matching BMC/storage state
Single fault-action record plus timestamped physical LED, BMC health, sensor, SEL, controller/array and host evidence
Reinsertion/replacement and controller recognition, rebuild/resync progress and completion, data/host checks and expected event clearing
Recovered healthy physical LED and BMC/storage state, unexpected-event review and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The row-802 Master procedure and criterion consistently target a health LED matching a healthy and fault state, though Expected Values are underspecified. Code reuse and the copied DeepSeek BurnIn overlay are disambiguated by Source Key and are prior-review/data-association defects, not an irreconcilable contradiction within this Master variant.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Exact LED values, transition timing, safe fault target and recovery are Project readiness inputs. The core target, physical action and acceptance direction are understandable, so the review is MANUAL ONLY rather than permanently blocked.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects the duplicate row's BurnIn/SSH method as zero coverage for this health-LED case.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its data-safety and evidence concerns but changes BLOCKED to MANUAL ONLY under the V3.1 distinction between missing execution inputs and irreconcilable semantics.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Uses the duplicate row evidence to correct its PARTIAL BurnIn association and restore the physical LED/manual boundary.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Keeps the manual classification while clarifying that duplicate identity is already resolvable and adds explicit LED timing, degraded-array and completed-rebuild acceptance.

review_improvement: Restores the actual health-indicator test, prevents an unrelated stress workload from claiming coverage, and makes the full data-safe fault-to-recovery sequence auditable without mislabeling missing Project values as permanent blocking.
independent_technical_reasoning: A CPU/memory/GPU/network burn-in can remain healthy and therefore cannot substitute for the specified health-state transition. The decisive evidence is a physical LED observation correlated to one known BMC/storage fault and its recovery. Those core actions require a person, but the missing exact color, timing and safe target can be supplied by Project SPEC, so they affect readiness rather than review completion.
